fact: The policy working group of the December 2025 ITU Africa Broadband Maps national event in Lusaka recognised the National ICT Policy as the overarching framework governing ICTs in Zambia.

TechAfrica News reports that on 12 November 2025 the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services launched guidelines it said were aligned with the 2023 National ICT Policy, treated as an existing national policy.

The Electoral Reform Technical Committee report, submitted 17 April 2025, describes the National ICT Policy 2023 as the policy framework expressing the Government's commitments for developing the ICT sector in Zambia; no separate adoption date is given, so the report date is used.

The National Assembly committee report states that the Government, in the National Information and Communication Technology Policy of 2006, set a goal of expanding the telecommunications backbone countrywide to widen access to ICT services; the year 2006 is the policy's date, not the report's.

The Ministry of Technology and Science published the National ICT Policy 2023, with a foreword by the Minister, as the government's revision of the 2006 National ICT Policy; the document gives no adoption date, so the published date of 11 October 2023 is used.
The full policy text is hosted on the Ministry of Technology and Science's own website as a PDF; the document gives no other date, so its published date is used.
The policy states no end year or period of validity; it is anchored on Vision 2030 but sets no term of its own (published date used).

Chapter 5 makes the Ministry responsible for ICTs responsible for policy coordination, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, with the Cabinet Office also monitoring and evaluating implementation and ZICTA regulating the sector (published date used).

The financing section lists the government national budget among seven possible sources, with bilateral and multilateral financing, FDI, private finance, capital markets and PPPs, and states no budget line or amount for the policy (published date used).

The plan states that Government has embarked on a review of the National ICT Policy, alongside the 2021 cyber security policy and four 2021 Acts; no adoption of a revised policy is stated (dated by the plan's publication, 2023-08-17).

The study states that in 2023 the National Digital Transformation Strategy, anchored on the National Information and Communication Technology Policy of 2023, was adopted; the document does not describe the policy's own scope.

The plan states that Government has embarked on a review of the National ICT Policy, among other ICT policy and legal reforms; it gives no date for the review, so the document's published year 2026 is used.
